Team —

Following up from our discovery call with BrightEdge this morning. They want a short, decision-ready set of supply scenarios we can commit to in the SOW that balance latency SLOs and cost. I attached their monthly traffic profile sample and a one-page forecast from their product team.

Ask: can you sketch three safety-stock scenarios we can present to the customer by EOD Monday? I want them in the form of:

- Scenario name (Conservative / Baseline / Aggressive)
- Required sustained node counts by region (US / EU / APAC) and the likely SKU mix (e.g., a100x4, h100x8, q8 variants)
- Burst lanes (minutes-hours) and how many spare slots we’d keep for deal-driven spikes
- Expected per-token cost delta and any pricing implications if they want guaranteed capacity
- Risk notes (cold-start latency, cross-region failover limits, data residency flags)

Attachments: 2026-07-30_BrightEdge_forecast_slide_deck.pdf, traffic_profile_sample.csv

Context: BrightEdge is targeting a paid pilot (1–2 months) for a high-throughput chat+embedding mix. They asked specifically about Singapore and Frankfurt residency for APAC/EU respectively.

If we can provide a quick matrix with recommended commitment bands + suggested contract language for burst clauses, that will speed legal/procurement.

Thanks —

Michael —

Outlined three quick scenarios below based on the traffic sample. I dropped a compact matrix into the shared Drive (scenario_matrix.xlsx) — link in the doc list. High-level:

1) Conservative (min commit)
- US: 8 x h100(8) nodes sustained (handles ~120K tokens/s steady for gen-heavy flows)
- EU (Frankfurt): 4 x a100(4) sustained (embedding-heavy, lower concurrency)
- APAC (Singapore): 2 x a100(4) sustained + 2 x burst-capacity h100(8) on-call
- Burst lanes: allow 30-minute burst at 2x sustained in each region with automatic billing uplift; keep 3 spare hot slots in US, 1 in EU, 1 in APAC
- Cost impact: ~+22% unit cost vs pure shared; adds a monthly committed base.
- Risks: can suffer 300–450ms additional cold-starts for cache-miss long-context sessions in APAC if burst nodes spin up.

2) Baseline (recommended for pilot)
- US: 12 x h100(8) sustained; EU: 6 x a100(4); APAC: 4 x a100(4) sustained + 2 x pre-warmed h100(8)
- Burst lanes: 1-hour bursts at 2.5x sustained, with 5 spare hot slots in US, 2 in EU, 2 in APAC
- Cost impact: ~+38% unit cost vs shared, but reduces tail-latency by pre-warming KV cache and keeping longer-lived contexts
- Notes: includes suggestion to enable per-route KV prefix caching for their largest prompt flows (can reduce token cost by ~12% in steady state)

3) Aggressive (SLA-backed)
- US: 20 x h100(8); EU: 10 x a100(4) + 2 h100(8) as hot reserve; APAC: 8 x h100(8) dedicated (pilot in SG)
- Burst lanes: 3-hour sustained burst agreements with guaranteed hot backstop; maintain 10 spare hot slots in US, 4 in EU, 4 in APAC
- Cost impact: ~+70% unit cost; recommended only if BrightEdge wants <100ms p50 for generation on multimodal, pretokenized inputs
- Risks: procurement timeline and committed spend may be a blocker for pilot.

Operational notes:
- For APAC pilot in Singapore, we recommend a 2-week warmup where we route a percentage of traffic to SG to pre-fill KV caches and measure tail latency
- If they insist on strict data residency, we will need a short addendum to SOW for localized audit logs and KMS keying in region

I’ll sync with Ops (Irene) to validate node counts against current free capacity and estimated procurement lead times.

-Karthik
Principal Capacity Planner
Redwood Inference

Sam / Priya —

Thanks — good questions. Quick replies inline and then a set of next steps.

1) Cold-start pre-warm windows:
- 4-hour pre-warm: reduces cold-start tail by ~40–50% (typical improvement from longer-lived KV cache hits), so you’d see cold-starts move into ~180–260ms range on average for APAC for most prompt sizes.
- 24-hour pre-warm: mostly eliminates cold starts for your observed nightly batch patterns; expect p95 generation latency similar to US p95 for identical prompts. The tradeoff is cost — you pay for longer sustained dedicated node time.

2) Security/residency checklist:
- SOC2: Redwood can provide scoped SOC2 coverage for the dedicated pool in SG/Frankfurt; delivery requires a short SOW addendum and regional KMS keying (we’ll provide a template).
- KMS: we support region-scoped KMS keys; ops will need the key ARN and to confirm key rotation windows. Irene will follow up with the exact doc set.

3) Baseline monthly committed est: (ballpark)
- Baseline (no burst option): $110k–$140k / month
- Baseline (with 1-hour burst option): $135k–$170k / month (burst premium ~20–25% depending on usage profile)

Next steps:
- Irene, can you validate node availability and confirm procurement lead times for SG and Frankfurt?
- Karthik, finalize the scenario_matrix.xlsx with SKU-level pricing inputs and a short paragraph for SOW burst language.
